message.content: why is the retry budget per-host and not global?

content.text:
A global budget lets one sick host starve every healthy one.

Each host gets its own token bucket, refilled at `retry_rate` per second. When a host
starts failing it burns its own tokens and stops retrying — the rest of the fleet never
notices.

```rust
fn should_retry(&self, host: &Host) -> bool {
    self.buckets.get(host).is_some_and(Bucket::take)
}
```

The budget is deliberately **not** shared with the circuit breaker: a breaker trips on a
host being down, a budget trips on retries being expensive. They fire at different times.

message.content: what happens when the bucket is empty but the request is idempotent?

content.text:
Nothing special — it fails like any other request.

Idempotency tells you a retry is *safe*, not that it is *free*. The budget exists because
retries cost the upstream, and an idempotent request costs it exactly as much as a
non-idempotent one.

| condition | retried | reason |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| tokens left, idempotent | yes | safe and affordable |
| tokens left, unsafe | no | replay risk |
| bucket empty | no | upstream is already paying |

> The budget is about the upstream's load, never about your correctness.

See `retry::Budget` for where the two checks meet.
